Assert that no rows match a condition

Source: R/expect_none.R
expect_none.Rd

The in-pipeline form of expect_empty(). Instead of filtering for the violations and piping them in, pass the condition directly. The check is the same, but data itself is returned, so the pipeline continues with all rows:

Usage

expect_none(
  data,
  ...,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL,
  log = getOption("daos.check_log"),
  dump = getOption("daos.check_dump")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

...

Conditions that describe a violating row, as in dplyr::filter().

success_msg

Message shown (and logged) when data is empty. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the log names every check that ran, and "The dataset is empty." otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown (and logged) when rows match and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the condition.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when data is not empty. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

log

Optional path to a log file. The directory is created automatically. Defaults to getOption("daos.check_log").

dump

Optional directory. When the check fails, the offending rows are written there as a timestamped CSV file (UTF-8 with BOM, so Excel reads æøå correctly). Defaults to getOption("daos.check_dump").

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

df |>
  expect_none(is.na(id), abort_msg = "Rows without an id") |>
  expect_none(amount < 0) |>
  mutate(...)

Conditions follow dplyr::filter() semantics: several conditions are combined with &, and a row where a condition is NA does not count as a violation. Test for missing values explicitly with is.na() when they matter.

Without a message, the condition itself becomes the message ("Found rows where amount < 0"), which is often clear enough during exploration. Write your own message for checks that stay in production.

See also

expect_empty(), expect_unique(), tally_violations()

Examples

ggplot2::mpg |>
  expect_none(cyl < 4) |>
  expect_none(hwy > 40, warn_msg = "Implausibly efficient cars") |>
  nrow()
#> ✔ No rows where cyl < 4
#> Warning: Implausibly efficient cars
#> ℹ 3 rows found:
#>   manufacturer = "volkswagen", model = "jetta", displ = 1.9, year = 1999, cyl =
#>   4, trans = "manual(...
#>   manufacturer = "volkswagen", model = "new beetle", displ = 1.9, year = 1999,
#>   cyl = 4, trans = "ma...
#>   manufacturer = "volkswagen", model = "new beetle", displ = 1.9, year = 1999,
#>   cyl = 4, trans = "au...
#> [1] 234

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
dplyr::starwars |>
  expect_none(is.na(species), abort_msg = "Characters without a species")
} # }
